summary: Steel fire tower on Brawley Mountain in Fannin County, no longer manned, closed to the public and used for antennas; build date not found.

facts.design: 50-foot steel tower with a 13-by-13-foot metal live-in cab, catwalk and flat roof
facts.status_note: Still standing, but the register says the cab is falling into disrepair.

access.note: First flight of steps removed to prevent access; N2Backpacking says it is no longer accessible to the public.

visit.trail_note: About 3.2 miles from Wilscot Gap on the Benton MacKaye Trail; a gated forest road (FR 45) also leads to the tower.

events.note: Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register February 19, 2019
Forest Service scoping for a proposed radio site beside the tower began July 28, 2021; the project is now marked Cancelled

notes_for_editor: Four sources, and none gives a build year or designer; a Chattahoochee National Forest history or a Blue Ridge Ranger District contact is the next step. Elevation differs by source: register 3,060 ft (933 m), N2Backpacking 3027 ft, and a Georgia tower list 3016 ft; the record's 932.7 m follows the register. Staffing is undated (Mountain Travel Guide). The closed status rests on the 2019 register entry and two undated web guides, so confirm with the Forest Service before presenting it as current. The record's access 'unknown' is now 'closed'.
